title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Adjudication of Cases Involving Disputes over New Plant Varieties
keywords_en: Intellectual Property; Court's initiation of dispute over new plant varieties
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Carrying out Trial Work of Cases Involving Disputes over New Plant Varieties

Fa [2001] No. 18

To: All High People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of the People's Republic of China came into effect on October 1, 1997. On April 23, 1999, China formally acceded to the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV) and undertook to fulfill the obligations under the Union's Convention. On June 16 and August 10, 1999, the agricultural part and the forestry part of the Rules for the Implementation of the Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of the People's Republic of China were respectively promulgated and implemented. The Ministry of Agriculture and the National Forestry Bureau, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, have been accepting applications for rights to new plant varieties from domestic and foreign entities since April 23, 1999, and have granted rights to new plant varieties to those applications that meet the requirements. Judicial protection of rights to new plant varieties is a new trial function conferred on the people's courts by national law and represents a new area in the intellectual property trial work of the people's courts. Properly carrying out this trial work will be conducive to establishing China's own advantages in new plant varieties and providing strong judicial protection for the rapid development of agriculture and forestry.

To ensure that the people's courts lawfully accept and fairly adjudicate on dispute cases involving the protection of new plant varieties, the Supreme People's Court has issued the Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Dispute Cases over New Plant Varieties. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows:

1. The trial of dispute cases over new plant varieties is a new task in the intellectual property trial work of the people's courts. All high and intermediate people's courts shall organize relevant trial personnel to carefully study and research the international conventions on the protection of new plant varieties, the regulations on the protection of new plant varieties and their implementing rules, and the judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court, to become familiar with and master relevant legal theories and professional knowledge, actively carry out internal and external business exchanges in this area, promptly summarize trial experience, and strive to improve the professional quality and law enforcement level of trial personnel.

2. Dispute cases involving new plant varieties belong to the category of intellectual property dispute cases and shall, in accordance with the provisions of Document Fa Fa [2000] No. 30 of the Supreme People's Court, be handled by the relevant trial division.

3. Active communication shall be maintained with the relevant administrative authorities, and research work on disputes over new plant varieties shall be actively carried out. For cases that have significant social impact, complicated facts, or difficulty in the application of law, the situation shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court on the basis of fact-finding. For final adjudications in cases involving disputes over new plant varieties, the legal documents shall be promptly submitted to the Third Civil Trial Division of the Supreme People's Court.

February 5, 2001
